subject: ipc
source: International Primary Curriculum (IPC), Milepost 3 thematic units (ages 9–12), Fieldwork Education; science content aligned to the English National Curriculum (Years 5–6)

weeks.topic: The Great, the Bold and the Brave — Entry point: what makes a leader?
objectives: Discuss qualities of great leaders
Compare leaders from history and today
Ask questions for the unit

weeks.topic: The Great, the Bold and the Brave — History: democracy in Ancient Athens
objectives: Describe how democracy worked in Ancient Athens
Compare Athens and Sparta
Explain who could and could not vote

weeks.topic: The Great, the Bold and the Brave — History: Alexander the Great
objectives: Describe Alexander's empire on a map
Evaluate whether Alexander was a good leader
Use sources to form a view

weeks.topic: The Great, the Bold and the Brave — History: the legacy of Ancient Greece
objectives: Identify Greek ideas that influence us today
Explore the Olympics, theatre and philosophy
Explain the meaning of legacy

weeks.topic: The Great, the Bold and the Brave — Society: brave leaders in modern times
objectives: Research a modern leader such as Nelson Mandela or Malala Yousafzai
Explain how they showed courage
Compare with ancient leaders

weeks.topic: The Great, the Bold and the Brave — Exit point: leadership presentations
objectives: Present a leader to the class
Explain why they are great, bold or brave
Reflect on our own leadership

weeks.topic: Saving the World — Entry point: our planet under threat
objectives: Identify environmental problems around the world
Discuss causes and effects
Share what we can do

weeks.topic: Saving the World — Science: adaptation, evolution and inheritance
objectives: Explain how animals and plants are adapted to their environment
Describe how living things have changed over time
Recognise that offspring vary and are not identical to parents

weeks.topic: Saving the World — Science: classifying living things
objectives: Classify living things into broad groups
Use classification keys
Give reasons for classifying based on characteristics

weeks.topic: Saving the World — Geography: endangered species and deforestation
objectives: Locate endangered species and their habitats
Explain the effects of deforestation
Explore the Amazon rainforest case study

weeks.topic: Saving the World — Exit point: environmental action campaign
objectives: Plan an environmental action for the school
Persuade others to take part
Evaluate the impact

weeks.topic: Brainwave — Entry point: how does our brain work?
objectives: Identify parts of the brain and their jobs
Explore how the brain controls the body
Share questions about learning

weeks.topic: Brainwave — Science: the nervous system and senses
objectives: Describe how messages travel through the nervous system
Investigate reaction times
Explain how the senses send information to the brain

weeks.topic: Brainwave — Learning: memory and how we learn
objectives: Explore how memory works
Try different memory strategies
Reflect on how we learn best

weeks.topic: Term 1 review: leaders, environment and the brain
objectives: Revisit key ideas from the Term 1 units
Explain scientific vocabulary
Reflect on learning goals

weeks.topic: Brainwave — Exit point: brain-friendly study habits
objectives: Create a guide to healthy study habits
Explain the effect of sleep, diet and exercise on the brain
Present the guide to younger pupils

weeks.topic: Investigators — Entry point: a crime scene mystery
objectives: Observe and record evidence at a mock crime scene
Ask scientific questions
Plan how to investigate

weeks.topic: Investigators — Science: fingerprints and classification
objectives: Take and classify fingerprints
Compare patterns: arches, loops and whorls
Use classification to identify suspects

weeks.topic: Investigators — Science: chromatography
objectives: Separate ink colours using chromatography
Compare results to identify a pen
Explain how separation works

weeks.topic: Investigators — Science: light and shadows
objectives: Explain that light travels in straight lines
Explain how we see objects by reflected light
Use shadows to work out shape and position

weeks.topic: Investigators — Exit point: solving the case
objectives: Analyse all the evidence collected
Present a conclusion supported by evidence
Evaluate the investigation

weeks.topic: Temples, Tombs and Treasures — Entry point: discovering Tutankhamun
objectives: Explore the discovery of Tutankhamun's tomb
Explain how archaeologists find out about the past
Ask questions about Ancient Egypt

weeks.topic: Temples, Tombs and Treasures — Geography: life along the Nile
objectives: Explain why the Nile was vital to Ancient Egypt
Describe farming and the flood cycle
Locate Egypt on a map

weeks.topic: Temples, Tombs and Treasures — History: pyramids, beliefs and mummification
objectives: Describe Egyptian beliefs about the afterlife
Explain how and why mummies were made
Explore how pyramids were built

weeks.topic: Temples, Tombs and Treasures — Art: hieroglyphics and Egyptian art
objectives: Explore hieroglyphics and the Rosetta Stone
Recognise features of Egyptian art
Create artwork in an Egyptian style

weeks.topic: Temples, Tombs and Treasures — Exit point: class museum exhibition
objectives: Curate a museum exhibition about Ancient Egypt
Write labels for artefacts
Guide visitors through the exhibition

weeks.topic: Mid-year assessment: IPC learning goals
objectives: Show knowledge from Term 1 and 2 units
Use scientific and historical vocabulary
Apply skills to new questions

weeks.topic: Moving Pictures — Entry point: the history of film and animation
objectives: Explore how moving images were first made
Place film inventions on a timeline
Watch and discuss early animations

weeks.topic: Moving Pictures — Science/Technology: light and optical toys
objectives: Explain persistence of vision
Make a zoetrope or flip book
Explain how light helps us see moving images

weeks.topic: Moving Pictures — Science: electrical circuits for a film set
objectives: Build circuits with switches, bulbs and buzzers
Use recognised circuit symbols
Explain how voltage affects brightness

weeks.topic: Moving Pictures — Exit point: class film premiere
objectives: Plan, film and edit a short animation
Present the film at a class premiere
Evaluate the finished film

weeks.topic: Moving On — Entry point: change and transition
objectives: Reflect on changes in our lives
Discuss feelings about moving to secondary school
Ask questions about the next step

weeks.topic: Moving On — Society: children's rights around the world
objectives: Explore the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child
Compare children's lives in different countries
Discuss responsibilities that come with rights

weeks.topic: Moving On — Personal: skills for secondary school
objectives: Practise organisation and independent study skills
Plan a timetable and homework routine
Set personal goals

weeks.topic: Moving On — Exit point: primary school memory project
objectives: Create a memory book or presentation
Celebrate achievements across primary school
Reflect on international mindedness

weeks.topic: End-of-year assessment: IPC learning goals
objectives: Show knowledge from the Year 6 units
Explain ideas with subject vocabulary
Apply skills to unfamiliar questions

weeks.topic: Year 6 IPC review and celebration
objectives: Reflect on IPC learning across Milepost 3
Share personal learning goals achieved
Prepare for Key Stage 3
